questions.q: Six rice bags at a ration shop weigh 24, 25, 25, 26, 27 and 29 kg, so their mean is 26 kg. A seventh bag weighing 33 kg is unloaded. What is the mean weight of the seven bags?
questions.a: 27 kg

questions.q:
The marks of four students are 11, 14, 17 and 26.
(a) Find the total distance from 16 of the marks below 16, and the total distance from 16 of the marks above 16. Is 16 the balancing point of the data?
(b) Using (a), say whether the mean is more or less than 16, then find the mean and check that it balances.
questions.a: (a) Below 16: (16 - 11) + (16 - 14) = 5 + 2 = 7. Above 16: (17 - 16) + (26 - 16) = 1 + 10 = 11. The two totals are unequal, so 16 is not the balancing point. (b) More distance lies above 16, so the centre must move up: the mean is more than 16. Mean = 68/4 = 17. Check: below 17 the distances are 6 + 3 = 9, above 17 the distance is 9, so 17 balances.
s: Part (a): totals 7 below and 11 above, so 16 is not the centre
Part (b): mean is more than 16; mean 17, with 9 = 9 on both sides

questions.q:
Assertion (A): If a value greater than the mean is removed from a data set, the mean of the remaining values is less than the old mean.
Reason (R): The total distance from the mean of the values below it equals the total distance from the mean of the values above it.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.q: A rain gauge recorded 4, 7, 9, 12, 15 and 20 mm on six days, so the median is 10.5 mm. One more day's reading is included and the median of the seven readings becomes 12 mm. Which of these could the new reading be?
questions.a: 16 mm

questions.q:
Gauri claims: 'Including a value greater than the median never lowers the median, and it always raises it.' Test both halves of her claim on two data sets, each time including the value 20:
Set P: 6, 8, 8, 8, 13
Set Q: 6, 8, 10, 13, 15
Then give your verdict on the claim.
questions.a: Set P: median 8. After including 20 the data is 6, 8, 8, 8, 13, 20 and the median is (8 + 8)/2 = 8, unchanged. Set Q: median 10. After including 20 the data is 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 20 and the median is (10 + 13)/2 = 11.5, which is higher. Verdict: partly right. The first half is correct: in neither set did the median fall, because a value above the median adds one more value on the upper side. The second half is wrong: Set P shows the median can stay the same when the middle values repeat, so 'always raises' fails.
s: Set P: median stays 8 after including 20
Set Q: median rises from 10 to 11.5
Verdict partly right: 'never lowers' holds, 'always raises' fails for Set P

questions.q: The data 5, 9, 10, 16 has mean 10. One more value is included and the mean becomes 12. The value included is ___. (Write the number in digits.)

A family's electricity bills for five months were Rs 1,240, Rs 1,180, Rs 1,320, Rs 1,450 and Rs 1,060; their mean is Rs 1,250. One bill turns out to be the neighbour's and is removed. The mean of the other four bills is Rs 1,267.50. Which bill was removed?

A data set has mean 30. Consider these statements.
I. Removing a value equal to 30 leaves the mean unchanged.
II. Including the two values 34 and 24 together raises the mean.
III. Including the three values 28, 27 and 35 together leaves the mean unchanged.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q: True or False: A data set has mean 40. If the two values 52 and 31 are included together, the mean increases. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. 52 is 12 above the mean and 31 is 9 below it. The extra distance above (12) is more than the extra distance below (9), so the balance shifts upward and the mean increases. (For example, if the data had 4 values, the sum would be 160 and the new mean (160 + 83)/6 = 40.5.)
s: States True
Compares the distances 12 above and 9 below, so the balance moves up

questions.q:
Class 8B has 30 students. Their mean height is 148.4 cm and their median height is 149 cm. In July three new students join the class, with heights 146 cm, 151 cm and 150 cm.
(a) For each new student, say whether the height is above or below the old mean, and by how many cm.
(b) Without finding the new mean, decide whether the class mean goes up, goes down or stays the same.
(c) Find the new mean height of the 33 students, correct to one decimal place.
(d) The class teacher says, 'Two of the three are taller than the old median, so the median must go up.' Decide whether the information given is enough to support her statement.
questions.a: (a) 146 cm is 2.4 cm below; 151 cm is 2.6 cm above; 150 cm is 1.6 cm above. (b) Total distance above = 2.6 + 1.6 = 4.2 cm, below = 2.4 cm, so the balance shifts up and the mean goes up. (c) Old total = 148.4 x 30 = 4452 cm; new total = 4452 + 146 + 151 + 150 = 4899 cm; new mean = 4899/33 = 148.5 cm (148.45...). (d) Not enough. The median cannot go down, but whether it rises depends on the middle heights of the old class, which are not given. If the 15th and 16th heights were both 149 cm, the new median (17th of 33) is still 149 cm; if they were 148 cm and 150 cm, it becomes 150 cm. So her word 'must' is not supported.
s: Part (a): 2.4 below, 2.6 above, 1.6 above
Part (b): 4.2 above against 2.4 below, so the mean goes up
Part (d): not enough information; the median may stay 149 or rise, so 'must' is not supported

questions.q:
Six parcels weigh 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 kg; their mean is 7 kg.
(a) Which one parcel must be removed so that the mean of the remaining five is 7.4 kg?
(b) Explain, using the balancing idea, why the parcel removed had to be lighter than 7 kg.
questions.a: (a) The five remaining must total 7.4 x 5 = 37 kg; the six total 42 kg, so the parcel removed weighs 42 - 37 = 5 kg. (b) The mean went up from 7 to 7.4. Removing a value below the mean takes away distance on the lower side, so the centre moves up; removing a value above 7 would have lowered the mean.
s: Part (a): 42 - 37 = 5 kg parcel removed
Part (b): the mean rose, which happens only when a value below the mean is removed

questions.q: Five friends scored 1, 3, 4, 9 and 13 in a quiz. Arjun wants the 'centre' of the scores: the number for which the total distance of the scores below it equals the total distance of the scores above it. Which number is it?
The data 15, 18, 21 has median 18. Show that no single value, however large, can be included so that the median of the four values becomes 22.
questions.a: With four values the median is the average of the 2nd and 3rd values when sorted. Whatever value v is included, the 2nd value is at most 18 and the 3rd value is at most 21 (if v is 21 or more, the sorted data is 15, 18, 21, v). So the new median is at most (18 + 21)/2 = 19.5. A very large v only sits at the end; it cannot push the middle past 18 and 21. Since 19.5 is less than 22, no single value can make the median 22.
s: States the new median is the average of the 2nd and 3rd of four sorted values
Shows the 2nd value is at most 18 and the 3rd at most 21, so the median is at most 19.5
Concludes 22 is impossible because a large value only goes to the end

questions.q:
A data set of 8 values has mean 50.
(a) Two values are included together, one of them 58, and the mean stays 50. Find the other value.
(b) Instead, three values are included: two less than 50 and one equal to 65, and the mean stays 50. Give one possible pair for the two smaller values, and state the condition every such pair must satisfy.
(c) Explain why including three values that are all greater than 50 can never keep the mean at 50.
(d) Instead, only the single value 74 is included. Find the new mean, correct to two decimal places.
questions.a: (a) 58 is 8 above 50, so the other must be 8 below: 42. (b) 65 is 15 above 50, so the two smaller values must together be 15 below 50, that is, their sum must be 2 x 50 - 15 = 85 with each less than 50; for example 45 and 40 (5 + 10 = 15). (c) Each value adds distance on the upper side and none adds distance on the lower side, so the balance can only move up; the mean must rise. (d) Old total = 50 x 8 = 400; new total = 474; new mean = 474/9 = 52.67.
s: Part (a): the other value is 42
Part (b): a valid pair such as 45 and 40
Part (b): condition: the two values sum to 85 (their distances below 50 total 15)
Part (c): all distances are on the upper side, so the mean must rise

questions.q: Six runners' scores in a school sports test, in order, are 31, 35, 40, 44, 52 and 58, so the median is 42. A latecomer takes the test and scores 47. What is the new median of the seven scores?

The data 12, 15, 18, 23, 32 has mean 20. Mira removes 32 from her copy; Kabir removes 12 from his copy.
(a) Without calculating, whose new mean is higher? Give the reason.
(b) Find both new means and the difference between them.
questions.a: (a) Kabir's. He removed a value below the mean, which raises the mean; Mira removed a value above the mean, which lowers it. (b) Mira: 68/4 = 17. Kabir: 88/4 = 22. Difference = 22 - 17 = 5.
s: Part (a): Kabir's, because removing a value below the mean raises it and removing one above lowers it
Part (b): 17 and 22, difference 5

questions.q: Dhruv claims: 'If one value below the mean is removed from a data set and one value above the mean is included in its place, the new mean must be higher than the old mean.' Test his claim on the data 6, 9, 12, 13 by replacing 9 with 10.5, and then say whether it holds for every data set.
questions.a: Old mean = 40/4 = 10. Replacing 9 (below 10) with 10.5 (above 10) gives 6, 10.5, 12, 13, with total 41.5 and mean 41.5/4 = 10.375, which is higher. Verdict: Dhruv is right for every data set. The number of values stays the same, and the total changes by (new value - removed value); the new value is above the mean and the removed one is below it, so this change is positive. The same count with a bigger total always gives a bigger mean.
s: Old mean 10; new data 6, 10.5, 12, 13
New mean 10.375, higher than 10
Verdict right in general: same count, total rises by (new - removed) > 0

questions.q:
A school kabaddi squad has seven players weighing 48, 52, 55, 57, 58, 61 and 68 kg. A reserve player weighing 54 kg is to replace exactly one of them.
(a) Find the mean and the median weight of the present squad.
(b) Find the new mean and median if the reserve replaces the 68 kg player.
(c) Which player must the reserve replace so that the mean weight falls by exactly 1 kg? Show your working.
(d) The coach wants the median to stay as it is now. Which players could the reserve replace? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) Total = 399 kg, mean = 399/7 = 57 kg; median (4th of 48, 52, 55, 57, 58, 61, 68) = 57 kg. (b) Total = 399 - 68 + 54 = 385 kg, mean = 55 kg; sorted 48, 52, 54, 55, 57, 58, 61, median = 55 kg. (c) A fall of 1 kg in the mean is a fall of 7 kg in the total, so the player replaced weighs 54 + 7 = 61 kg. (d) The 48, 52 or 55 kg player. Swapping a weight below 57 for 54 (also below 57) keeps three weights below 57 and three above, so 57 stays in the middle; replacing 57 or any heavier player puts four weights below 57 and makes the median 55.
s: Part (a): mean 57 kg and median 57 kg
Part (b): mean 55 kg and median 55 kg
Part (c): total must fall by 7 kg
Part (c): the 61 kg player is replaced
Part (d): the 48, 52 or 55 kg player, with the below/above count reason

questions.q:
Rekha timed five laps of the school track: 62, 58, 65, 60 and 70 seconds. Their mean is 63 s. She then ran a sixth lap in 57 s and wrote in her notebook: 'New mean = (63 + 57) / 2 = 60 s.'
(a) Explain what is wrong with her method.
(b) Find the correct mean of the six laps.
(c) Find the median of the six laps.
(d) Her coach will pick her for the relay if either the mean or the median of all her laps is under 61 s. She may run one more (seventh) lap; she has never run a lap faster than 57 s. Should she ask to run it? Justify using what each measure needs.
questions.a: (a) She averaged the old mean with one new value, as if the old mean were a single lap. The old mean stands for five laps, so the 57 s lap is only one of six values; the mean must be total time divided by 6. (b) Total = 315 + 57 = 372 s, mean = 372/6 = 62 s. (c) Sorted: 57, 58, 60, 62, 65, 70, so the median is (60 + 62)/2 = 61 s. (d) Yes. For the seven-lap mean to be under 61 s the total must be under 61 x 7 = 427 s, so the seventh lap must be under 427 - 372 = 55 s, faster than she has ever run. But the seven-lap median is the 4th value: any seventh lap of 60 s or less makes it 60 s, and a lap between 60 s and 61 s makes it that lap time. So any lap under 61 s, which she has managed three times already (57, 58, 60), gets her picked through the median.
s: Part (a): the old mean represents five laps, so averaging it with one value is wrong
Part (c): median (60 + 62)/2 = 61 s
Part (d): Yes; the mean needs a lap under 55 s, but any lap under 61 s brings the median under 61 s

questions.q: The marks of a class have mean 25 and median 22, and no two students have the same marks. A late student's mark of 24 is included. What happens to the mean and the median?
o: The mean falls and the median rises
Both the mean and the median rise
Both the mean and the median fall
The mean rises and the median falls
questions.a: The mean falls and the median rises

questions.q:
The data 4, 9, 12, 15, 21, 30, 33 has median 15.
(a) Exactly two values are to be removed and the median must stay 15. What rule must the two removed values follow?
(b) Would removing 4 and 9 keep the median at 15? Find the new median.
questions.a: (a) Remove one value from below 15 and one from above 15 (not 15 itself), so 15 still has the same number of values on each side. (b) No. Removing 4 and 9 leaves 12, 15, 21, 30, 33, whose median is 21.
s: Part (a): one value below 15 and one above 15
Part (b): No; new median 21

questions.q: True or False: If every value in a data set of 12 values is increased by 5, the mean of the data set increases by 60. Give the reason or the corrected statement.
questions.a: False. The total increases by 12 x 5 = 60, but the total is then divided by the same 12 values, so the mean increases by 60/12 = 5. Corrected statement: the mean increases by 5 (and the total by 60).
s: States False
Corrects it: the total rises by 60 but the mean rises by only 5

questions.q: A PT teacher measured the heights of 32 students and found the mean to be 151.6 cm. Later she noticed that all of them had worn school shoes, and each pair adds 1.5 cm to a student's height. What is the correct mean height?

Assertion (A): The mean of the first 40 odd numbers 1, 3, 5, ..., 79 is 40.
Reason (R): The mean of the first 40 odd numbers is double the mean of the first 40 counting numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 40, which is 20.5.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.a: A is true but R is false

questions.q:
Let x1, x2, x3, ..., xn be n values whose mean is a.
(a) Show, using algebra, that if every value is multiplied by 4 and then 7 is subtracted from it, the new mean is 4a - 7.
(b) Use (a) to find the new mean when this rule is applied to the data 12, 15, 9, 20, 14.
(c) Apply the rule to each value and check your answer to (b) directly.
(d) Find the new mean if the steps are done in the other order (subtract 7 first, then multiply by 4), and say why it differs from (b).
questions.a: (a) New mean = [(4x1 - 7) + (4x2 - 7) + ... + (4xn - 7)]/n = [4(x1 + x2 + ... + xn) - 7n]/n = 4(x1 + ... + xn)/n - 7n/n = 4a - 7. (b) Old mean = 70/5 = 14, so the new mean = 4 x 14 - 7 = 49. (c) New data 41, 53, 29, 73, 49; total 245; mean 245/5 = 49, which matches. (d) (14 - 7) x 4 = 28. In this order the 7 is also multiplied by 4, so 28 is subtracted from 4a instead of 7: 4(a - 7) = 4a - 28.
s: Part (a): writes the new mean as a sum over n and separates 4(x1 + ... + xn)/n
Part (a): simplifies to 4a - 7
Part (b): old mean 14, new mean 49
Part (c): new values 41, 53, 29, 73, 49 with mean 49
Part (d): 28, because the 7 is also multiplied by 4

questions.q: A fruit seller sells a mean of 18 kg of mangoes a day at Rs 60 per kg. Every day she also earns a fixed Rs 40 for home delivery. What are her mean daily takings?

Assertion (A): If every value in a data set is increased by 6, the median also increases by 6.
Reason (R): If every value in a data set is increased by 6, the mean increases by 6.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q:
The mean length of 8 ribbons is 1.35 m.
(a) Write the mean length in centimetres.
(b) A tailor cuts 12 cm off every ribbon. Find the new mean length in centimetres and the new total length of the 8 ribbons.
questions.a: (a) Multiplying every length by 100 multiplies the mean by 100: 1.35 x 100 = 135 cm. (b) Subtracting 12 cm from every ribbon subtracts 12 from the mean: 135 - 12 = 123 cm. New total = 123 x 8 = 984 cm.
s: Part (a): 135 cm
Part (b): new mean 123 cm and new total 984 cm

questions.q: A data set has mean 20. The same change is made to every value. Which change does NOT give a new mean of 30?
questions.a: Add 5, then multiply by 2

questions.q: Imran claims: 'If every value in any data set is increased by Rs 10, the mean also increases by 10%.' Test his claim on the amounts Rs 40, Rs 50 and Rs 90, and then give your verdict, saying for which data sets it would happen to work.
questions.a: Old mean = 180/3 = Rs 60. Adding Rs 10 to every value adds Rs 10 to the mean, so the new mean is Rs 70. The rise is 10 out of 60, which is about 16.7%, not 10%. Verdict: Imran is wrong. Adding a fixed amount raises the mean by that amount, not by that percentage; a rise of Rs 10 is 10% only when the old mean is Rs 100. (A 10% rise of every value would mean multiplying every value by 1.1.)
s: Old mean Rs 60 and new mean Rs 70
The rise is 10/60, about 16.7%, not 10%
Verdict wrong: adding 10 adds 10 to the mean; it is 10% only when the old mean is 100

questions.q:
A data set has mean 12. Match each change made to every value with the new mean.
Column A:
1. Add 3 to every value
2. Multiply every value by 3
3. Subtract 3 from every value
4. Multiply every value by 3, then subtract 3
Column B:
(P) 9
(Q) 33

A school weather club recorded the noon temperature for six days: 21, 19, 24, 18, 22 and 22 degrees C. A week later they found that their thermometer always showed 1.5 degrees C more than the true temperature.
(a) Find the mean of the recorded temperatures.
(b) Find the correct mean without correcting each reading. State the rule you used.
(c) Find the correct median temperature.
(d) Before finding the fault, the club had printed a poster saying 'Typical noon temperature: 21.5 degrees C' and 'Hottest minus coldest day: 6 degrees C'. Which of the two lines must be reprinted? Justify using your answers.
questions.a: (a) Total = 126, mean = 126/6 = 21 degrees C. (b) Subtracting the same number from every value subtracts it from the mean: 21 - 1.5 = 19.5 degrees C. (c) Sorted recorded values 18, 19, 21, 22, 22, 24 give median (21 + 22)/2 = 21.5; every value falls by 1.5 and the order is unchanged, so the correct median is 20 degrees C. (d) Only the 'typical temperature' line. 21.5 degrees C was the recorded median; the correct median is 20 degrees C, so that line is wrong. The hottest (24) and coldest (18) readings both fall by 1.5 to 22.5 and 16.5, so their difference stays 22.5 - 16.5 = 6 degrees C, and that line is still correct.
s: Part (a): mean 21 degrees C
Part (b): 19.5 degrees C, using 'subtract k from every value, subtract k from the mean'
Part (c): recorded median 21.5, correct median 20 degrees C
Part (d): reprint only the typical-temperature line (20, not 21.5); the difference stays 6 since both ends drop by 1.5

questions.q:
A data set has mean a. The same steps are applied to every value. Consider these statements.
I. Subtracting 4 from every value and then adding 4 to every value leaves the mean as a.
II. 'Multiply by 3, then add 3' gives the same new mean as 'add 1, then multiply by 3'.
III. 'Halve, then add 5' gives the same new mean as 'add 5, then halve'.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and II only

questions.q:
Five friends have Rs 40, Rs 55, Rs 60, Rs 70 and Rs 75; the mean is Rs 60. Their grandmother gives each of them Rs 15 more.
(a) By how much does the total amount increase?
(b) Use the fair-share idea of the mean to explain why each friend's fair share rises by exactly Rs 15, and state the new mean.
questions.a: (a) The total rises by 5 x 15 = Rs 75. (b) If the money were pooled and shared equally, the extra Rs 75 would be split among the same 5 friends, so each share grows by 75/5 = Rs 15. The new mean is 60 + 15 = Rs 75.
s: Part (a): total rises by Rs 75
Part (b): Rs 75 shared among 5 gives Rs 15 more each; new mean Rs 75

questions.q: Every value in a data set was multiplied by 4 and then increased by 2, and the new mean is 50. Tara works back as 50 / 4 - 2 = 10.5 and says the old mean was 10.5. Which statement is correct?
o: 12, because 2 must be subtracted before dividing by 4
10.5, because her order of undoing the steps is right
13, because 2 must be added back before dividing by 4
12.5, because the added 2 makes no difference to it
questions.a: 12, because 2 must be subtracted before dividing by 4

questions.q:
The data 10, 16, 22 has mean 16. Each value is changed by one fixed rule and the new mean is 28. Ravi says the rule was 'add 12'. Sita says the rule was 'multiply by 2, then subtract 4'.
(a) Show that both rules give a new mean of 28.
(b) Write the new data under each rule.
(c) Can the new mean alone tell us which rule was used? What else in the new data would tell them apart?
questions.a: (a) Add 12: 16 + 12 = 28. Multiply by 2 then subtract 4: 2 x 16 - 4 = 28. (b) Ravi's rule: 22, 28, 34. Sita's rule: 16, 28, 40. (c) No, both give mean 28. The gaps differ: adding 12 keeps the gaps between values at 6 (the values only slide along), while multiplying by 2 doubles the gaps to 12.
s: Part (a): both rules give 28 from the old mean 16
Part (c): No; adding keeps gaps of 6, doubling makes gaps of 12

questions.q:
A tuition centre has five batches whose monthly fees are Rs 1,200, Rs 1,350, Rs 1,500, Rs 1,650 and Rs 1,800. To pay a new teacher, the mean fee must rise to at least Rs 1,620. Three plans are proposed.
Plan A: raise every fee by Rs 150.
Plan B: raise every fee by 8%.
Plan C: raise every fee by 5% and then add Rs 50.
(a) Find the old mean fee and the new mean fee under Plan A.
(b) Without working out each new fee, find the new mean fee under Plan B and under Plan C.
(c) Find how much more the Rs 1,200 batch would pay each month under each plan.
(d) Parents of the lowest-fee batch ask for the smallest possible increase for their batch. Which plan should the centre choose so that it still meets the Rs 1,620 target? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Old mean = 7500/5 = Rs 1,500. Plan A: 1500 + 150 = Rs 1,650. (b) Plan B multiplies every fee by 1.08, so the mean becomes 1500 x 1.08 = Rs 1,620. Plan C multiplies by 1.05 and then adds 50, so the mean becomes 1500 x 1.05 + 50 = Rs 1,625. (c) Plan A: Rs 150. Plan B: 1200 x 0.08 = Rs 96. Plan C: 1200 x 1.05 + 50 = 1310, so Rs 110. (d) Plan B. All three plans reach a mean of at least Rs 1,620 (1,650, 1,620 and 1,625), and among them Plan B gives the Rs 1,200 batch the smallest increase, Rs 96 against Rs 110 and Rs 150. It meets the target exactly, with no margin, but the target says 'at least', so it is enough.
s: Part (a): old mean Rs 1,500, Plan A Rs 1,650
Part (b): Plan B Rs 1,620 and Plan C Rs 1,625 from the mean
Part (c): increases Rs 150, Rs 96 and Rs 110
Part (d): Plan B: meets the target and gives the smallest increase (Rs 96)

questions.q:
Nine students recorded how many times they rode their cycles in one week: 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9.
(a) Find the mean and the median for this week.
(b) Next week every student rides 2 more times than this week. Without listing the new data, find next week's mean and median.
questions.a: (a) Total = 27, mean = 27/9 = 3; median (5th value) = 2. (b) Adding 2 to every value adds 2 to the mean and, since the order does not change, to the middle value too: mean 5, median 4.
s: Part (a): mean 3 and median 2
Part (b): mean 5 and median 4

questions.q:
(a) By pairing the first and last numbers, the second and second-last, and so on, find the mean of the 30 counting numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 30.
(b) Use (a) to find the mean of the first 30 multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, ..., 180.
(c) Use (a) to find the mean of the 30 numbers 5, 11, 17, ..., 179 (each is 1 less than a multiple of 6).
(d) Ali says, 'Multiplying by 6 moves the mean up by 6, so the mean in (b) is 6 more than the mean in (a).' Find the real difference and explain his mistake.
questions.a: (a) The pairs 1 + 30, 2 + 29, ..., 15 + 16 are 15 pairs, each summing to 31; total = 465, mean = 465/30 = 15.5. (b) Each multiple is 6 times a counting number, so the mean is 6 x 15.5 = 93. (c) Each number is 6n - 1, so the mean is 6 x 15.5 - 1 = 92. (d) Real difference = 93 - 15.5 = 77.5, not 6. Ali confused multiplying with adding: adding 6 to every value raises the mean by 6, but multiplying every value by 6 multiplies the mean by 6.
s: Part (a): 15 pairs of 31, mean 15.5
Part (d): real difference 77.5
Part (d): Ali used the adding rule for a multiplying change

questions.q: A test was marked out of 40 and the class mean was 26. The teacher converts every mark to a mark out of 100 by multiplying it by 2.5, and then adds 3 grace marks to every converted mark. What is the new class mean?

Data set P is 3, 7, 8, 14 and data set Q is 103, 107, 108, 114.
(a) Find the mean of P, and use it to write the mean of Q without adding the values of Q.
(b) Compare the total distance of the values below the mean, and above the mean, in P and in Q. What does this show about where the mean sits?
questions.a: (a) Mean of P = 32/4 = 8. Every value of Q is 100 more, so the mean of Q is 108. (b) In P: below 5 + 1 = 6, above 6. In Q: below 5 + 1 = 6, above 6. The distances are exactly the same, so the mean keeps the same position relative to the data; the whole picture has just slid 100 along.
s: Part (a): mean of P 8, mean of Q 108
Part (b): distances 6 and 6 in both, so the mean's relative position is unchanged

questions.q: Write a real-life situation in which the new mean of a data set is found by the rule: new mean = 12 x old mean + 500. Say what each value stands for, what the 12 and the 500 mean, and find the new mean when the old mean is 250.
questions.a: Example: In a class, each student saves the same amount every month all year, and the mean monthly saving is Rs 250. At the end of the year every student also gets Rs 500 as a Diwali gift and adds it to her savings. questions.q:
A school library counts its student visitors each day. For one week the register shows: Monday 52, Tuesday 38, Wednesday (smudged), Thursday 45, Friday 61, Saturday 40. The mean for the six days is 47.
(a) Find Wednesday's count.
(b) Find the median number of visitors for the six days.
(c) The library will get a new book rack if the mean over seven days (these six days and Sunday, a reading-fair day) is at least 48 visitors. Find the least number of visitors needed on Sunday.
(d) The fair organiser expects about 56 visitors on Sunday, but rain is forecast, and on rainy days about 1 in 10 of the expected visitors usually stay away. Should the librarian tell the students that the rack is as good as certain? Give a reason with numbers.
questions.a: (a) Six-day total = 47 x 6 = 282. Known days add up to 52 + 38 + 45 + 61 + 40 = 236, so Wednesday = 282 - 236 = 46. (b) Sorted: 38, 40, 45, 46, 52, 61, so the median is (45 + 46)/2 = 45.5. (c) Seven-day total needed = 48 x 7 = 336, so Sunday needs at least 336 - 282 = 54 visitors. (d) No. 56 is only 2 more than the 54 needed. If 1 in 10 stay away because of rain, about 56 - 5.6 = 50.4, that is about 50, will come, which is short of 54. The rack is possible but not certain; she would need about 60 expected visitors (54 is 9/10 of 60) to be safe even with rain.
s: Part (a): Wednesday 46
Part (b): median 45.5
Part (c): at least 54 visitors on Sunday
Part (d): No; with rain about 50 come, below 54, so it is not certain

After 9 innings in a school cricket series, Smriti's mean score was 42 runs.
(a) Find her total runs after 9 innings.
(b) After her 10th innings her mean rose to 45. How many runs did she score in the 10th innings?
(c) In the 11th innings she scored 12. Find her mean after 11 innings.

Part (b): 72 runs
Part (d): needs 540 in all, so 78 in the 12th innings

In a plastic-bottle recycling drive, Classes 6 to 10 of a school collected bottles. The notice board shows a mean of 84 bottles per class, but Class 9's number is torn off. The others are: Class 6: 62, Class 7: 75, Class 8: 99, Class 10: 103.

(b) Classes 11 and 12 then join the drive, and the mean for all seven classes becomes 88. Find the total collected by Classes 11 and 12 together.
(c) Class 12 collected 14 bottles more than Class 11. Find each class's count.
(d) Every class that collected more than the seven-class mean gets a certificate. How many classes get one? Name them.
questions.a: (a) Five-class total = 84 x 5 = 420; known = 62 + 75 + 99 + 103 = 339; Class 9 = 420 - 339 = 81. (b) Seven-class total = 88 x 7 = 616, so Classes 11 and 12 together = 616 - 420 = 196. (c) Class 11 = (196 - 14)/2 = 91, Class 12 = 105. (d) Above 88 are Class 8 (99), Class 10 (103), Class 11 (91) and Class 12 (105): 4 classes. Class 9 (81), Class 6 and Class 7 do not.

questions.q:
The data 14, 31, 9, 26, 40, 22, q has median 26.
(a) Which of these could be q: 20, 26, 35, 50? Explain.
(b) If instead we were told the mean is 24, how many values could q take? Find it.
(c) Use (a) and (b) to say how finding an unknown value from the median differs from finding it from the mean.
questions.a: (a) Sorted without q: 9, 14, 22, 26, 31, 40. With q there are 7 values and the median is the 4th. If q is 22 or less, the 4th value is 22; if q is between 22 and 26, the 4th value is q itself, so the median is q, not 26; if q is 26 or more, the 4th value is 26. So 26, 35 and 50 work, and 20 does not. (b) Total = 24 x 7 = 168; the six known values add up to 142, so q = 26: only one value. (c) The mean fixes the unknown exactly because it uses the total, while the median only needs the unknown to lie on the correct side of the middle, so many values are possible.
s: Part (a): 26, 35 and 50 work; 20 makes the median 22
Part (b): q = 168 - 142 = 26, a single value
Part (c): mean gives one value from the total; median allows a whole range

questions.a: (a) 1x2 + 2x3 + 3x7 + 4x9 + 5x5 + 6x4 = 2 + 6 + 21 + 36 + 25 + 24 = 114 throws. (b) 114/30 = 3.8 throws. (c) Running totals: 2, 5, 12, 21, 26, 30. The median is the average of the 15th and 16th values; both lie in the '4 throws' group (positions 13 to 21), so the median is 4. (d) Fewer than 3.8 means 1, 2 or 3 throws: 2 + 3 + 7 = 12 students, which is 12/30 = 2/5 of the students.
s: Part (a): 114 throws

questions.a: (a) Total of values = 3 + 2f + 15 + 8 = 26 + 2f and the count is 10 + f. So (26 + 2f)/(10 + f) = 2.4, giving 26 + 2f = 24 + 2.4f, so 0.4f = 2 and f = 5. (b) Frequencies 3, 5, 5, 2 (15 values); running totals 3, 8, 13, 15. The median is the 8th value, which is 2.
s: Part (a): equation (26 + 2f)/(10 + f) = 2.4 solved to f = 5

questions.a: (a) 8A: 0 + 2 + 8 + 24 + 24 + 20 = 78, mean 78/25 = 3.12. 8B: 0 + 3 + 6 + 12 + 28 + 25 = 74, mean 74/25 = 2.96. (b) Both medians are the 13th value. 8A running totals 1, 3, 7, 15: the 13th is 3. 8B running totals 3, 6, 9, 13: the 13th is 3. Both medians are 3. (c) 8A: more than 3.12 means 4 or 5 marks: 6 + 4 = 10 students. 8B: more than 2.96 means 3, 4 or 5: 4 + 7 + 5 = 16 students. (d) 8B's total would rise by 3 x 2 = 6 to 80, mean 80/25 = 3.2, which is higher than 8A's 3.12. So the teacher's statement is supported: those three low scores pull 8B's mean below 8A's.
s: Part (a): means 3.12 and 2.96
Part (b): both medians 3
Part (c): 10 students in 8A and 16 in 8B
Part (d): 8B's new total 80, mean 3.2
Part (d): 3.2 is above 3.12, so the teacher is supported

questions.q: A frequency table shows value 3 with frequency 6, value 4 with frequency 2 and value 5 with frequency x, where x is a whole number (it may be 0). Show that the mean of this data can never be 3.2.
questions.a: With x = 0 the mean is (18 + 8)/8 = 26/8 = 3.25, which is already above 3.2. Every value of 5 added is greater than the current mean, and including a value greater than the mean raises the mean, so as x grows the mean only rises above 3.25. So the mean is at least 3.25 and can never be 3.2. (Algebra agrees: (26 + 5x)/(8 + x) = 3.2 gives 1.8x = -0.4, which is not a whole number.)
s: Mean with x = 0 is 3.25
Each extra 5 is above the mean, so the mean only rises
Concludes the mean is never below 3.25, so 3.2 is impossible

Arun was asked to find the mean and median. He wrote: 'There are 5 rows. The middle row is 2 books, so the median is 2. Mean = (0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4)/5 = 2.'

(b) Find the correct median using running totals.

questions.a: (a) Total = 0 + 4 + 12 + 30 + 32 = 78 books; mean = 78/30 = 2.6. (b) Running totals 2, 6, 12, 22, 30. The median is the average of the 15th and 16th values, both in the '3 books' group (positions 13 to 22), so the median is 3. (c) He took the middle row of the table, which ignores how many students are in each row; the median is the middle student, found from the running totals. Part (b): running totals and median 3

questions.q:
A shop sold 40 school T-shirts in March. The sizes sold were: size 28 (6 shirts), size 30 (10), size 32 (14), size 34 (7), size 36 (3).
(a) Find the mean size sold.
(b) Find the median size sold.
(c) In April the shop sold exactly the same numbers of each size, except that size 36 sold 13 shirts instead of 3. Find the mean and the median size for April.
(d) The shopkeeper's rule is: 'I will order size 36 in bulk for May only if April's mean size is above 32 and at least a quarter of April's customers bought size 36.' Use your April figures to decide whether he should place the bulk order, and say how close the decision is.
questions.a: (a) Total = 28x6 + 30x10 + 32x14 + 34x7 + 36x3 = 168 + 300 + 448 + 238 + 108 = 1262; mean = 1262/40 = 31.55. (b) Running totals 6, 16, 30, 37, 40. The 20th and 21st values are both 32, so the median is 32. (c) April: 50 shirts, total = 1262 + 36 x 10 = 1622, mean = 1622/50 = 32.44. Running totals 6, 16, 30, 37, 50; the 25th and 26th values are both 32, so the median is still 32. (d) Yes, but only just. April's mean size is 32.44, which is above 32, and 13 of the 50 April customers bought size 36, which is 13/50 = 26%, just above a quarter (25%, that is 12.5 shirts). Had one fewer size 36 shirt been sold (12 of 49, about 24.5%), the second condition would have failed. Note that the median stayed at 32, so the higher mean comes only from the extra size 36 shirts.
s: Part (a): mean 31.55
Part (b): median 32
Part (c): April mean 32.44
Part (c): April median still 32
Part (d): both conditions met (32.44 > 32 and 13/50 = 26% >= 25%), so order, though only just

questions.q:
An eco-club records the kilograms of waste paper collected by four houses over five weeks. Row 1 holds headings, rows 2 to 5 hold Red, Blue, Green and Yellow houses, and columns B to F hold Weeks 1 to 5:

(b) Write the formula to type in D6 for the average collected per house in Week 3, and give its value.

questions.a: (a) =SUM(B2:F2); 12 + 15 + 9 + 14 + 10 = 60 kg. (b) =AVERAGE(D2:D5); (9 + 16 + 11 + 12)/4 = 12 kg. (c) Totals: Red 60, Blue 62, Green 64, Yellow 61, so Green collected the most. Part (b): =AVERAGE(D2:D5), value 12

Rohan logs his daily steps in a sheet. Cells B2 to G2 hold Monday to Saturday: 6800, 7200, 8100, 7600, 6900 and 8400. H2 held Sunday's steps, and I2 holds =AVERAGE(B2:H2), which showed 7600. Then H2 was deleted by mistake.

(d) Rohan has never walked more than 9500 steps in a day. Can he reach the target by changing only Sunday? If not, and he walks 9500 on Sunday, how many extra steps must he add on each of Monday to Saturday (the same number each day)?
questions.a: (a) 7 cells (B, C, D, E, F, G, H). (b) Total = 7600 x 7 = 53200; Monday to Saturday add up to 45000, so H2 was 53200 - 45000 = 8200. With 9500 on Sunday the total is 54500, which is 1500 short; spread over 6 days that is 1500/6 = 250 extra steps each day.
s: Part (a): 7 cells
Part (b): H2 was 8200
Part (c): at least 11000 on Sunday

Part (b): each segment steeper than the last, the increase grows by 1 cm a week

(a) Explain how the 'monthly average rainfall for July' of a city, shown on a line graph, is worked out from rainfall records.
(b) A city's July rainfall in four years was 610 mm, 540 mm, 720 mm and 650 mm. What value would the graph show for July?
questions.a: (a) The total rainfall in July is recorded for several years, and these July totals are averaged. (b) (610 + 540 + 720 + 650)/4 = 2520/4 = 630 mm.
s: Part (a): the July totals of several years are averaged
Part (b): 630 mm

questions.q:
A line graph shows the number of new rooftop solar connections each year in a district and in two of its blocks, P and Q:
District: 2019: 1,800; 2020: 2,400; 2021: 4,000; 2022: 6,500; 2023: 8,800; 2024: 9,600
Block P: 600; 900; 1,500; 2,800; 4,100; 4,300
Block Q: 500; 700; 1,200; 1,900; 2,600; 2,900
(a) By how many did the yearly new connections grow from 2019 to 2024 in Block P and in Block Q? Which block's line rises more over the six years?
(b) Between which two consecutive years is the district line steepest?
(c) What fraction of the district's new connections were in Block P in 2019? Was Block P's share larger or smaller in 2024?
(d) A reporter writes, 'The district line is much less steep from 2023 to 2024 than from 2022 to 2023, so fewer new connections were made in 2024 than in 2023.' Find the mistake and correct the statement.
questions.a: (a) Block P: 4,300 - 600 = 3,700. Block Q: 2,900 - 500 = 2,400. Block P's line rises more. (b) Yearly rises: 600, 1,600, 2,500, 2,300, 800, so 2021 to 2022 is steepest. (c) 600/1,800 = 1/3 in 2019. In 2024 it is 4,300/9,600, about 0.45, which is larger than 1/3. (d) A less steep rising segment means a smaller increase, not a decrease. New connections still went up, from 8,800 to 9,600; only the increase was smaller (800 against 2,300). Correct: 'More new connections were made in 2024 than in 2023, but the increase was much smaller.'
s: Part (a): growth 3,700 in P and 2,400 in Q; P rises more
Part (b): 2021 to 2022 (a rise of 2,500)
Part (c): 1/3 in 2019, larger (about 0.45) in 2024
Part (d): a less steep rise is a smaller increase, not a fall
Part (d): corrected statement with 9,600 > 8,800 and rises 800 vs 2,300
